variantPolicy: Seeded variants alter traffic shape, pool headroom, workload concurrency, and external-state ambiguity; they are not independent published assets.

exercises.title: Build a Cross-Signal Incident Timeline
exercises.objective: Identify leading, coincident, and downstream signals without claiming causality from one graph.
exercises.initialState: Synthetic checkout SLIs, JVM metrics, pool metrics, traces, logs, and change events cover the same twenty-minute window.
exercises.prompt: Construct the causal timeline, rank three hypotheses, and state falsification evidence under the supplied traffic and pool variant.
exercises.deliverable: Timeline, hypothesis table, confidence, falsifiers, and next query.

hints.text: Ask which signal changed before checkout latency.
Separate resource occupancy from time spent waiting.
Use the request trace to connect symptoms to the shared resource.

exercises.referenceSolution: Anchor on checkout success, align traffic and resource windows, show pool borrow wait leading request delay, use traces/backtraces to associate the custom workload, reject JVM saturation with pre-incident metrics, and list evidence that would disprove the contention hypothesis.

exercises.title: Repair a Defective Database-Heavy CronJob
exercises.objective: Redesign and test a customer extension that consumes unsafe shared database capacity.
exercises.initialState: A custom export uses unbounded parallel workers, overlapping transactions, no cancellation checkpoints, and page size 100.
exercises.prompt: Propose the bounded implementation and write a target-runtime test matrix for concurrency, abort, restart, failure, and checkout interference.
constraints: no direct database tuning as first fix
exercises.deliverable: Implementation design, unit tests, platform integration tests, load test, failure injection, and evidence manifest.

hints.text: Treat pool headroom as a shared capacity budget.
Test interruption between page completion and checkpoint persistence.
Assert checkout outcomes while the job runs, not only export throughput.

exercises.referenceSolution: Use bounded workers and short read transactions, stable keyset pagination, durable checkpoints and cancellation checks; prove unit logic, target-runtime persistence behavior, injected interruption, restart correctness, representative load, shared-pool headroom, and checkout SLIs.

exercises.title: Design an Actionable Checkout Alert
exercises.objective: Detect customer impact early and attach discriminating evidence without universalizing synthetic thresholds.
exercises.initialState: The current alert uses only a fixed checkout p95 threshold and pages during planned changes.
exercises.prompt: Specify SLI, baseline, multi-window trigger, context panels, maintenance handling, ownership, and validation for the supplied traffic profile.
exercises.deliverable: Alert contract, dashboard context, runbook link, and test plan.

hints.text: Page on impact; diagnose with context.
Use maintenance context without hiding unexpected failure.
Test the alert against a known synthetic incident and a harmless traffic spike.

exercises.referenceSolution: Use checkout success, error, and tail latency with traffic-aware multi-window thresholds; attach pool wait, worker, JVM, dependency and change context; preserve privacy-safe diagnostics; link ownership and runbook; validate against positive and negative fixtures.

exercises.title: Write the Saturation Incident Runbook
exercises.objective: Turn the investigation into a safe, role-aware, testable operational procedure.
exercises.initialState: Operators can access Cloud Portal, Dynatrace, logs, and supported Backoffice administration, but not hosts or the managed database.
exercises.prompt: Write trigger, triage, evidence, containment, escalation, recovery, reconciliation, communication, and closure steps for the supplied ambiguity level.
constraints: identify permitted actor for every action
no direct database or host action
exercises.deliverable: Versioned runbook with decision gates and evidence checklist.

hints.text: Put irreversible or support-required actions behind explicit gates.
A job stop is containment, not proof of recovery.
Include the evidence required to reconcile ambiguous payments.

exercises.referenceSolution: Define evidence-first triage, named command, supported custom-job containment, prohibited and support-required actions, duplicate protection, payment/order reconciliation, sustained technical and business checks, escalation package, communication cadence, and closure criteria.

exercises.title: Conduct the Post-Incident Observability Review
exercises.objective: Convert the incident into measurable diagnostic and workload controls.
exercises.initialState: Service recovered after the custom export stopped; existing monitoring detected impact late and no load gate covered job overlap.
exercises.prompt: Produce causal analysis and prioritize controls for the supplied recurrence and capacity assumptions.
constraints: controls require owners and effectiveness measures
do not claim universal platform limits
exercises.deliverable: Causal tree, corrective-action portfolio, residual risk, and review metrics.

hints.text: The manual start triggered the event; explain why one job could consume checkout capacity.
Measure prevention and detection controls separately.
Retest under overlapping business and batch load.

exercises.referenceSolution: Identify unbounded custom concurrency as the mechanism and weak workload governance, capacity testing, and alert context as contributors; add bounded design, overlap tests, capacity budgets, earlier business alerts, a tested runbook, owned measures, and explicit residual risk.
